chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Don Kirkpatrick, Lloyd Phillips and the Harlem arranging teacher
summary: Danny recalls arrangers Kirkpatrick and Lloyd Phillips, and an elderly Harlem music-theory teacher whose name he cannot recall.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: He's around there now. I went to New York twice and saw him a little bit.
Is still alive?
Yeah, he's in the phone book. But he lives with Don Kirkpatrick's wife, I think.
Mmm-hmm.
Do you know Don Kirkpatrick? The piano player that worked with Don Redman and Chick Webb? A tall old guy...
No, I can't place him.
Barker - II-74
Unassuming. He was a hell of a musician and a hell of an arranger.
No, I can't place him.
Well, he was fantastic. He died. You remember Lloyd Phillips?
Oh yeah. Lloyd was a very good piano player.

Well, them two was together. They'd stand on the corner, man, until daybreak every morning when they was working, and talk about arranging. They this old... What's this old, quiet man who used to teach everybody arranging? He looked like a little White man. He'd come to your house and he'd teach. What's that new arranger they had?
Sheridan(?)?

Yeah. This little old colored man. Everybody in Harlem went to him. He was supposed to be the mostly highly rated mathematician of music, the calculation of what resolved into this and what resolved into that, how you can resolve this -- and they'd sit up there and talk with him until the morning.
Is that right? I don't remember that, Danny. I wish I knew who that was.
Well, when you get back there, check about this guy in Harlem who used to teach. Like that boy Gene and them probably could tell you.
Barker - II-75
Gene Michael(?)...

Gene Michael(?) could tell you who this man was. He'd come to your house, and then give them a lesson. A calculation on how this resolved into this, like a checker...like chess. This resolves into that, and it's resolved into this, and there was a calculation of how you do every... Him and Lloyd Phillips used to talk every night.
Lloyd was a fabulous piano player.
